reviews.comment: best professor I've had at TAMU. Sure he's not the most tech savvy, and a little hard to hear, but if you make an effort in his class—he surely will in return. He offered help sessions EVERY WEEK outside of class hours that many students didn't take advantage of. He cares about the students & teaching the topics he's passionate about. Much respect!

Very knowledgeable but, lectures are extremely boring and repetitive, he uses an outdated version of LEED (2009), struggles to hear the students, takes forever to hand back grades, tries to teach us basic life skills even though it is a level 400 class, never stuck to the lesson plan. This class would be much more useful if someone else taught it.

He is honestly the best professor I've had at A&M, he is so knowledgable and caring about his students. He revolves this class around LEED certification so you learn so much stuff that you can actually apply in your future (if this interests you). He does get repetitive on some stuff but that just helps you learn it more! He's very accessible also.

Prof Culp definitely knows his stuff and if you pay attention and genuinely try, there is some serious content takeaway from this class. While his lectures can occasionally get repetitive, It means a lot to him that students participate in lectures. Minor criticism: he didn't hand back any grades during the semester and due dates often shifted.
